instruction: Resize the berries image to 640 pixels wide and 480 pixels tall.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully boosted image contrast by opening Colors > Brightness-Contrast dialog, setting contrast to 40, and applying. Completed in 9 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GIMP menus (Colors menu), use adjustment dialogs (Brightness-Contrast), set numeric values in fields, click OK to apply changes, understands image editing concepts.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different GIMP operation (Image > Scale Image) using the same setup. Resize is a related but different image manipulation skill that uses a different menu path and dialog.
metadata.explanation: Task requires resizing the image to 640x480 using GIMP's Scale Image dialog. Postconfig exports the modified image as berries_resized.png. Evaluator uses official check_image_size metric to verify dimensions match expected 640x480.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction requires resizing to 640x480; evaluator checks exactly width=640 and height=480 via check_image_size — full coverage.
Getter vm_file correctly fetches the exported file from /home/user/Desktop/berries_resized.png.
Metric check_image_size receives the rules dict directly (width, height) and accesses them correctly via rule.get('width') and rule.get('height').
Postconfig uses Shift+Ctrl+E (Export As) to save the current GIMP canvas state, ensuring the resized image is written to disk before the getter fetches it.
Expected values (640, 480) are semantically correct and match the instruction exactly.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The postconfig writes filename 'berries_resized' without explicit extension — GIMP Export As dialog may default to .png based on the original file, but the behavior depends on the export dialog's default format selector. If the dialog doesn't auto-append .png, the file path could mismatch. Consider using 'berries_resized.png' explicitly in the pyautogui.write call.

Minor: The pyautogui.write call does not first clear the filename field (e.g., Ctrl+A before typing), so the typed name may append to any pre-filled filename rather than replacing it. Consider adding a select-all step before typing the new filename.
